problems.answer: I start by understanding how your business runs today. Then I design and build the smallest piece of technology that makes a real difference — and connect it to what you already use.

solutionsIntro.title: Five ways I can help your business.
solutionsIntro.intro: Most projects fit one of these — many combine two. Not sure which is yours? That's normal. Start with the problem.

solutions.label: AI Solutions
solutions.title: Put AI to work inside your actual business.
solutions.body: Not a chatbot bolted onto your homepage. AI that knows your documents, products and processes — and does useful work with them: answering questions, drafting replies, sorting requests and finding information in seconds.
problems: Staff spend hours searching documents, emails and old chats for answers.
Customers ask the same questions all day.
You have plenty of data but no quick way to ask it anything.
examples: AI features in your existing product

solutions.label: AI Automation & Integrations
solutions.title: Let the repetitive work run itself.
solutions.body: I map how work moves through your business today — the copying, checking, chasing and reminding — then connect your tools and let automation and AI handle the steps that don't need a person.
problems: The same data is typed into several systems.
Your CRM, shop, inbox and spreadsheets don't share information.

solutions.label: Websites & E-Commerce
solutions.title: A website that earns its place in your business.
solutions.body: Your website is often the first conversation a customer has with you. I build sites and online stores that make the offer clear, earn trust quickly and make the next step — buying, booking or getting in touch — easy.
problems: Visitors arrive but don't contact you or buy.
The site is slow, dated or hard to update.
Your store needs features your platform doesn't offer out of the box.

solutions.label: Custom Web Applications
solutions.title: When generic software doesn't fit your workflow, build software that does.
solutions.body: Generic tools make your team work their way. A custom web application works yours — one place for orders, bookings, stock, customers or internal operations, with exactly the screens and rules your business needs.
problems: You pay for several tools and still need spreadsheets to fill the gaps.
Important processes live in one person's head or inbox.
Customers or partners need their own secure access.

solutions.label: Mobile Applications
solutions.title: Put your service in your customers' pocket.
solutions.body: An app makes sense when people use your service often, on the move, or need their phone for it — notifications, camera, location. I build iOS and Android apps connected to your existing systems, so the app and the business stay in sync.
problems: Customers book, order or check status by phone call or message.
Field staff work from paper or WhatsApp.
You have an app idea and need it designed, built and launched.

work.title: Real projects, explained as problems and solutions.
work.intro: A few things I've built. No invented clients or numbers — just what was built and what it does.

items.name: WhatsApp Automation Bot
items.problem: Deliver useful daily updates to people on WhatsApp without anyone sending them by hand.
items.solution: A Node.js service that pulls live weather data and daily quotes from external APIs, fills message templates and sends them on schedule through the Twilio WhatsApp API.
items.result: Runs unattended: messages are fetched, composed and delivered automatically every day.

items.name: Car Info Lookup
items.problem: Get a vehicle's make, model, year and details quickly, from nothing more than a licence plate.
items.solution: Two native apps — Swift for iOS, Java for Android — that query vehicle data through an external API and present it in a consistent interface on both platforms.
items.result: A working lookup flow on both platforms, suited to verification, parking and quick-reference use.

items.name: Networking — Social Platform
items.problem: A platform where people can post, follow each other and message in real time.
items.solution: A full-stack web application with secure sign-up and login, feeds, likes, comments, follow notifications and real-time direct messaging over WebSockets.
items.result: Deployed on Vercel, with authentication, live notifications and messaging working end to end.

items.name: Go Nature — Park Management
items.problem: Park services needed one system for administrators and visitors instead of separate manual handling.
items.solution: A client-server Java system on a shared database, with separate interfaces for administrators and visitors and real-time communication between them.
items.result: A working multi-user system, built with a five-person team.

items.q: I know my problem but not what solution I need. Can you help?
items.a: That's the most common starting point — and the best one. Describe what's slowing you down or what you want to achieve. I'll suggest the simplest solution that would work, which is sometimes smaller than you expect.

items.q: Can you integrate AI into our current systems?
items.a: Usually, yes. If your systems offer an API, an export or database access, AI can often be connected to them — for example to read incoming requests, search your documents or draft replies. I check what your current tools allow before recommending anything.

items.q: Can you work on an existing project?
items.a: Yes. Adding features, integrating new tools or modernising part of an existing website or app is often faster and cheaper than a rebuild. I review what you have first and tell you honestly which option makes sense.

items.q: Do you build both websites and applications?
items.a: Yes — websites, online stores, web applications, and iOS and Android apps. When a project needs more than one, they can share the same backend so everything stays in sync.

items.q: Can you integrate Shopify, CRM systems and APIs?
items.a: In most cases. Connecting tools through their APIs, webhooks or automation platforms is a core part of what I do. Some systems are more open than others, so I confirm what's possible early on.

items.q: How much does a project cost?
items.a: It depends on scope, so I don't publish fixed prices. After a short conversation about what you need, you get a clear estimate before any work starts. Starting with a smaller first phase is often a good way to prove the value.
Focused work — a single automation or a landing page — is usually measured in weeks. Larger platforms and apps take longer. You get a realistic timeline together with the estimate.

items.q: Can you work with our internal team?
items.a: Yes. I can work alongside your developers, designers or operations team, taking on a defined part of the project or the parts that need a specific skill.

items.q: Do you provide support after launch?
items.a: Yes. Support, fixes and improvements after launch can be arranged around what your solution needs. Many projects continue with small improvements once real usage shows what matters most.
Yes, including right-to-left languages such as Arabic and Hebrew. This page itself is available in English, Arabic and Hebrew.
